newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GM Holden records A$243 mln year net profit.
newsitem.headline: GM Holden records A$243 mln year net profit.

text.p: General Motors' Australian subsidiary, General Motors Holden Australia, said on Monday it made a net profit of A$243 million for calendar 1996 down from an unaudited A$260 million for in 1995.
Holden said in a statement the earnings after tax and outside equity interests were generated from revenues of A$2.9 billion, representing a return on sales of 8.3 percent.

In 1995, Holden reverted to a calendar year reporting period and, at the time, estimated an after tax profit of A$260 million for the calendar year, on estimated total revenue of A$3 billion, an 8.6 percent return on sales, it said.

Holden chairman and managing director James Wiemels said the strong profit performance was achieved in an environment of rapidly rising imports and falling tariffs and was essential to the continuation of the company's ambitious investment agenda.

He said the very tough and demanding operating environment, defined by tightening margins and increasing market fragmentation, had continued into 1997 "with a commensurate impact on earnings so far this year".
The closing years of the century were shaping up to be the most challenging and dramatic period of change in the company's history, he said.
"However we look forward to that future, no matter how uncertain with confidence and commitment," he said.

Wiemels said 1996 was the first year in a five-year A$1.4 billion investment program aimed at allowing Holden to play a prominent role in the global plans of its parent, General Motors, particularly in the Asia Pacific area.
He welcomed the Australian government's recent decision to delay tariff cuts, saying it provided the company with the confidence to approach GM with its regional strategy.
The statement showed Holden's capital expenditure for 1996 was A$289 million, up on A$91 million the previous year.
